newsitem.title: JAPAN: Hard to see rapid fall in yen-Japan bankers' chief.
newsitem.headline: Hard to see rapid fall in yen-Japan bankers' chief.

text.p: The chairman of the Federation of Bankers Associations of Japan, Shunsaku Hashimoto, told a news conference on Tuesday that it was difficult to imagine a rapid fall in the yen from its current level.
He also said that Japan's long-term interest rates were likely to remain at low levels for a while, although he added that he expects them to move in parallel with the country's economic situation.
"Taking account of current (economic) fundamentals, it is difficult to imagine that the current weak yen trend will accelerate," he said.

Hashimoto said current low long-term interest rates would not affect Japan's economic recovery prospects in the latter half of 1997/98. He said the current situation reflected the short-term economic outlook for the April-June period and the demand/supply situation for bonds.

"I expect the rates to continue at the current low levels for a while, but in the long term they will move in parallel with the economic situation, as indicated in the interest-rate futures market," he said.
Hashimoto, who is also president of Sakura Bank Ltd, told the news conference his bank had been asked by Nippon Credit Bank Ltd to buy new shares it plans to issue.
He said NCB had asked Sakura to reply to the request by early May.
He said Sakura would make its decision after scrutinising NCB's restructuring programme and balance sheet and taking into account the overall stability of Japan's financial system.
